answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by selling a capped onyx witness each epoch. To enroll, an agent locks a bond and starts a lantern: a signed pulse from a unique hardware clock, published every few minutes. Graders verify the pulse chain and assign the key a single knoll in a sparse Merkle map; any reuse of that clock fingerprint or map slot is slashed, with the bond paid to the finders. Because the mint quota is fixed, each extra fake identity requires its own witness at a rising clearing price plus a fresh bond, so forgery costs scale at least linearly.
